content:
I would like to add a result stating that a functor F : C ⥤ D is an equivalence if and only if the induced functor on skeletons F.mapSkeleton : Skeleton C ⥤ Skeleton D is the functor of a categorical isomorphism IsoCat (Skeleton C) (Skeleton D).

I also have a related statement packaging this together with the bundled-equivalence formulation into a List.TFAE.

Would results of this form be suitable for mathlib, and does CategoryTheory/Skeletal.lean seem like the right place for them?

I previously opened PR #42789 for this, but it was closed because of new-contributors using LLM-generated code; before considering a new PR, I wanted to ask here first whether the statement and placement seem appropriate. If so I would write codes by hand and open a new PR.

From a mathematical point of view, this seems like a natural characterization to me: it makes precise the idea that an equivalence is exactly a functor that loses no information up to isomorphism. In fact, this is the perspective I usually use when introducing equivalences to students in category theory.
Instead of saying “The present version looks good to me.” when people make comments, maybe following experts suggestions from @Joël Riou would be better if you want your code in Mathlib

About the code itself, I was implicitly referring to the @.... followed by many _.
In terms of the mathematical organization, I think that the most important result is that a functor between skeletal categories is an equivalence iff it is an isomorphism, and this should be proven first.
Thanks. I'm going to work on that now.

Joël Riou said:

In terms of the mathematical organization, I think that the most important result is that a functor between skeletal categories is an equivalence iff it is an isomorphism, and this should be proven first.

I have a question. I found out the old API

noncomputable def Equivalence.skeletonEquiv (e : C ≌ D) : Skeleton C ≃ Skeleton D

can be upgraded to

noncomputable def Equivalence.skeletonIsoCat (e : C ≌ D) : IsoCat (Skeleton C) (Skeleton D)

What's mathlibs' overall opinion about how to deal with the old/new weak/stronger APIs?
e.g.

  1. delete the old one and fix the downstream dependence (I prefer this one);
  2. redefine old API as an API derived from the new API by one simple [Iso to Equiv] API and fix downstream dependence;
  3. keep the old API and provide a proof for the compatibility with the new API.

Or should we deal with this in a separate PR? I mean it does not affect the present PR.
define the old one in terms of the new one and deprecate it, fix uses downstream
I think this should be in a separate PR
Ok I agree it should be in a separated PR.
